narrative: Washed ashore, you have only vague recollections of what happened. The past seems unimportant now. Shivering, you watch the bodies float among the debris. No ships can be seen on the horizon.

parameters: There is nothing here but sand and gravel. Or so it may seem. You feel a painful sensation in your left foot, causing you to take a step backwards. Glimmering in the sun, a sharp object is revealed.

At first, you are unable to make sense of it. You pick it up to get a closer look. It’s a large, oval-shaped silver brooch, the kind that people use to fasten their cloaks. Something about the unusual design seems familiar.

A voice echoes in your mind. “It's a stingray.” Sculpted in the center, the exotic sea creature evokes memories of turmoil and suffering. There was a ship, a caravel was approaching. The stingray was emblazoned across the dark sails. Strangely, your memories seem garbled and distant.

label: Put the silver brooch in your pocket

parameters: You hide the silver brooch within the folds of your tattered rags. Tears come to your eyes. You're overwhelmed by feelings of relief, gratitude and confusion. Merely moving the symbol out of sight produced such an intense emotional reaction. How could it be? What could these people possibly have done to you?
You discover footprints in the sand, leading north. It’s late in the afternoon. If there’s another survivor out there, you should find this person before it gets dark.
They are somewhat small and delicate. You arrive at the conclusion that they were made by a person below average height, walking barefoot.

narrative: Something near the water has caught your attention, prompting you to take a quick look. Closer scrutiny reveals a rusty knife. While hardly ideal, it's better than nothing.

label: Take the knife and move on

narrative: Aside from the moldy mattress, the loft is empty.
The camp is empty. There are still faint traces of blood on the ground.
Having inspected the galley, you arrive at the conclusion that no less than thirty able-bodied rowers would be required to navigate this vessel across the ocean.
Ato Triasteen the deserter guards the ship with his long bow. "No trouble, so far. I'll remain vigilant until you've assembled the others. Time is of the essence."
Further north, the beach gives way to a flourishing wetland. You discover a lagoon, surrounded by red pines. At this point, there are no more footprints.
The lagoon has a certain quality of sacred tranquility. Reeds whisper in the spring breeze. Deflected by the scattered pines, the harsh winds travel elsewhere.

parameters: The lagoon is encircled by reeds, thick like palisades. You find a conspicuous opening near the shallows.

The lagoon is littered with dead bodies and driftwood. A few crates and barrels are floating around. New arrivals from the shipwrecked caravel, just like you. Time and time again, you tremble at the sight of the stingray, as each container has been marked with the same repulsive symbol.
Far too numerous and bloated beyond recognition, the dead bodies might as well be left undisturbed.
You spend some time with this, until you grow weary. Thankfully, there are a few things worth keeping.

narrative: Something is moving through the reeds on the other side. A wild dog emerges. Growling, it runs towards you across the shallows.

parameters: Whimpering, the wild dog collapses. Slowly, the carcass starts to drift into the lagoon.

narrative: Someone has been here quite recently. A pile of bloody bandages have been discarded on the worktable in front of you. There's also a hunting knife on the table, along with a pouch of assorted food rations. Facing the northern forest, there's a small window next to a ladder.
This place reeks of mold and ancient dust.

parameters: You catch a glimpse of a strange individual. Dressed in a green cloak and armed with a spear, the young man disappears into the forest.
Like a framed painting, the pine forest is perfectly serene.

narrative: There's a loft up here. Covered by dust and cobwebs, an old book lies next to a moldy mattress.
When you open the door, you notice a wild dog lurking outside. It's growling, yet keeps its distance, perhaps anticipating your next move.

parameters: You have slain the wild dog. The animal lies on the ground, bleeding and twitching.

label: Ignore the dog and walk away

parameters: Barking incessantly, the animal seems perplexed by your indifference. After a while, it scurries off into the wilderness.

narrative: Crossing a bridge over a stream, you realize that you are being watched. Armed with spears, two women observe you from a distance. They are dressed in green cloaks and blue tunics. Shortly after you've spotted them, they swiftly move out of sight.
You walk all the way back to the southern outskirts of the forest. As far as you can tell, there is no one following you.

label: Go back to the old shack

narrative: Seemingly without end, the winding path takes you deep into the forest. The pines are now enveloped by the shimmering light of golden dusk. Smoke is rising from a campfire in the distance.

The bloodstained footprints lead to another path through the forest. Forging ahead, you are faced with increasingly rugged terrain. Forced to constantly walk uphill, you lose yourself on the northern highlands, now obscured by the veil of night.

parameters: Your eyes adjust to the merciful darkness of spring. The full moon provides further assistance. The owls remind you that one is never truly alone in the forest. Despite the fact that you are left with neither path nor footprints to follow, you refuse to give up.

Rising above the others, a dark hill looms in the distance. The tranquility of the forest is disrupted by the ancient clang of war. Echoes of clashing metal ring out from the summit, marking the onset of battle.
Merely a brief eruption of violence, it seems. The echoes fade into silence when you reach your destination.
A trail of dead bodies guides your ascent. Disarmed and mutilated, their pale apparitions are uncanny. Whoever these people were, they share no similarities with the other forest dwellers.

Their faces are concealed by wooden masks, elaborately sculpted to resemble the beaks of ravens. Wearing nothing but loincloths and sandals, their athletic bodies are exposed, yet covered by intricate, matching patterns of feathers, which have been carved into their skin with dark inks.

narrative: The forest is shrouded in darkness.

You enter a moonlit grove on top of the hill. Exuberant cherry blossoms form a perfect circle around the meadow. The grass is darkened by the entrails of numerous corpses. A woman stands alone in the center, breathing heavily.
A full-scale war has erupted in the forest. The armies of cultists and druids clash on the highland battlegrounds. Venturing further south at this moment would be too risky.
The grove reeks of death. Their descent illuminated by the full moon, a growing parliament of rooks devour the flesh of those who masquerade as ravens.
The night is still young. More rooks arrive to join the great banquet.

parameters: While nomads are adaptive by nature, it's still baffling to see how comfortably Rasleen is able to rest on this meadow of putrid decay. Waving dismissively, she groans: "unless it's urgent, shut your trap."

narrative: You remove the white wooden mask from one of the corpses. There is nothing special about the lifeless face that you have uncovered. Admittedly, the raven mask itself is well crafted.
Gaping like an open wound, the ominous gateway beckons. The bridge will take you across the rift valley to the ruins of Dusk Megalith.
The sandstone bridge will take you across the rift valley.

parameters: A connection between two hills, the sandstone bridge is the only way to access the heights of Dusk Megalith. Surrounded by ruins above the elevation of rugged terrain, standing stones rise from the summit.
You glance across the northern ocean to your left. The rift valley is darkened below the high arches. A meandering, shallow stream disappears among the pines to the south.

narrative: It's too dark in here. You need a torch.

parameters: You explore the cavern by torchlight. The flickering flames reveal a staircase, spiraling down into the lower depths.

narrative: The sunlit walkway of Port Spire is empty. A druid warship is anchored at the far end of the clandestine harbor.
The bearded man heads upstairs, leaving you alone in the filthy dormitory. You can hear the loud echoes of his wooden clogs from the staircase.
The first floor dormitory is empty, aside from old junk and broken furniture.
The dark entryway to the underground prison is currently unguarded. The prison gate is open.
There's an old grave behind the shack, marked by a simple wooden board.

parameters: Slightly askew, the wooden grave marker is surrounded by weeds and sunflowers. The inscriptions are no longer legible.

narrative: You patrol the area. Having circled halfway along the edges of the grove, you hear something. Sounds like movement through the undergrowth.

parameters: Pale apparitions emerge between the cherry blossoms. It seems like the Apostles of Woe have sent reinforcements.

The rooks scatter in droves when the invasion begins. Forcing you to retreat, the masked swarm floods the grove from all directions. Rasleen bellows: "By the Great Wolf, we have to fight our way out! Grab a weapon from the pile if you need one!"
A masked cultist is rushing towards you, swinging a hatchet.
Blood gushing from her throat, the masked warrior dies apathetically. Having stepped over the fresh corpse, you manage to catch up with Rasleen. She is locked in battle with three cultists.

Catching the enemy by surprise, you deliver a savage strike to the gut, weakening the masked maceman. Having diverted his attention, you now stand face to face with this brutish cultist on the battleground.
Maneuvering swiftly, you creep up from behind and strike the knife-wielding cultist between the shoulder blades. Wounded, she turns around to face you with two daggers.

Blood, teeth and jaw fragments cascade when the brute falls like a ruinous tower. Simultaneously, Rasleen impales one cultist and decapitates another. The two of you have now breached an opening in the wall of hostile flesh, momentarily allowing you to slip away between the cherry blossoms.

Reduced to a lifeless bag of bones, she is quickly buried underneath the dismembered cultists who follow suit. Having mounted a severed head on her spear, Rasleen makes a run for it. It's now or never.

narrative: It's a big pile of rusty old weapons. Take your pick.
Rasleen is about to clash with several cultists. There's no time to lose.

parameters: As you rush to her aid, your path is intercepted by a masked swordsman.
Impervious to pain, the cultist quietly collapses when the loss of blood has taken its toll.

As you make haste across the battleground, you catch a glimpse of a weak, elderly cultist in the corner of your eye. The old geezer appears to be unarmed, yet his menacing demeanor suggests that he is about to take aim. It boggles the mind.
From what you can tell, he's holding some kind of flask.

Charging ahead, your bravery is rewarded with a sudden explosion, reducing your face to a smoldering heap of ash. The unknown alchemical agent has an acrid fragrance, permeating the brief agony of your last moment in this world.
Having kept an eye on him, you anticipate the incoming projectile. The flask explodes nearby as you tumble forward. Unscathed, you can smell the acrid fragrance of the unknown alchemical agent.
Whatever the nature of his nefarious plans, you were lucky enough to escape. Instead, you cross paths with a lumbering brute. The masked warrior in front of you is armed with a halberd.
The hunchback tries to escape, which only hurts him in the long run, as you manage to graze him a few times during the chase.
The brute crumbles like a pile of bricks. Rasleen has cleared the way ahead. It's time to go.

Another stoic figure spills his entrails on the meadow, in this case marking the conclusion of a long life. Rasleen retreats towards your position, quickly neutralizing a few cultists with a sequence of well-placed spear thrusts. Thus, a path now lies open, if only for the briefest moment.

narrative: Chased by a horde of cultists, you and Rasleen defy death in more ways than one, dashing rapidly down the northern slope. It's all a blur, from which you miraculously emerge with all bones intact.

parameters: Pines are split in half by the impact of bronze spears that rain down from the summit. Clouds of poison dust disperse like bursting puffballs. Splashing water as you run across a stream in the rift valley, your movement is sustained by the rush of adrenaline.

narrative: The two of you cautiously advance towards the ruins on the other side. You notice the embrasures on the wall.

parameters: Halfway across the bridge, Rasleen suddenly collapses. Struck down by an arrow, the nomad squirms near the precipice. As you may have feared, there is an archer hiding somewhere behind the fortifications of the ruinous pylon.

You turn around to escape. Several arrows cripple your legs. Staggering, you become an easy target, eventually falling off the bridge like a confused porcupine. You face death in the rift valley below.
Dismissively, Rasleen growls: "Don't worry about me!"

narrative: You run across the bridge, narrowly avoiding the projectiles. Having entered the ruins of Dusk Megalith, you confront the archer. She pulls out a dagger from her cloak and leaps forward to attack.

parameters: The young druid was no match for your martial prowess. Staggering through the entrance, Rasleen approaches. "This is bad, really bad." Coughing, she kneels down to grab the bow.
"Got hit by a poison-tipped arrow. You gotta find the antidote, or I'm dead, simple as that. I'll stay behind, for now…"
"And find the damned ship too, while you're at it. Good luck." Armed with the bow, she retreats to the fortified position previously occupied by the young archer.

label: Explore the ruins of Dusk Megalith

narrative: Having walked through the narrow archway, you discover the antechamber to a hall of crypts.
You have entered the antechamber to a hall of crypts.

parameters: Most of the crypts are sealed shut. However, a few of them can be accessed, their doors crumbled by the ravages of time.
You increase your wealth in the dusty old crypts.

narrative: Ominous and guttural, a deep growl echoes in the catacombs. Mane glistening, a black lion emerges from the shadows. Menacing, the ferocious creature approaches.

parameters: One last roar echoes in the catacombs when the black lion collapses.
There is no escape. With ease, the black lion intercepts your path to the staircase. Roaring, the creature leaps at you. You feel pain when the talons rip your torso.

narrative: When you remove the lid, a cloud of poison dust is released from the sarcophagus.

label: Close your eyes and hold your breath

parameters: You are unable to resist the adverse effects of the poison cloud, instead forced to endure immeasurable torment.
You are left unaffected by the poison cloud.
You're too slow. Coughing violently with tears running down your cheeks, you gradually come to your senses as the poison cloud is dispersed around you.
You swiftly avoid the poison cloud. Now that the dust has been dispersed, it should be safe to approach the sarcophagus.

label: Wait for the cloud to disperse

narrative: You discover the hallways of ancient catacombs. It's dark and quiet down here.
It's dark and quiet in the catacombs.

parameters: A plethora of sarcophagi are lined up along the walls. A dark tunnel lies ahead.
There is no discernible way to open these massive stone caskets, with the sole exception of one damaged sarcophagus.
You discover the mummified remains of an ancient druid. Arms crossed, the face is adorned with a white mask.
You remove the death mask from the mummified remains in the broken sarcophagus.
It's a dead end. The ceiling has collapsed. The floor is littered with the bone fragments of previous intruders. It seems like these unfortunate souls have left a few trinkets behind.
Old equipment, most of it useless.

narrative: You hear the ocean. The passageway is illuminated by sunlight.
You explore the cavern by torchlight. The flickering flames reveal a staircase, spiraling down into the lower depths.

Crumbled walls form a partial enclosure around the neglected garden, which is home to a variety of exotic flowers and common weeds. The path leads to another cavern. A druid stands guard near the entrance. Fortunately, he is not aware of your presence.
You walk the garden path near the temple ruins.

parameters: A few pillars remain intact, but the ancient temple has been reduced to a pile of rubble. There is nothing of interest here.

narrative: The camp is empty. There are faint traces of blood on the ground.
Momentarily blinded by primeridian sunlight, you walk down the stairs to the eastern plateau. You are faced with a garden path, meandering its way towards the ruins of the ancient temple.
Rooks descend from clear blue skies to devour the eyes of the slain druid. The entrance to the dark cavern is unguarded.
Ruinous walls form a partial enclosure around the temple garden on the eastern plateau.
You walk the garden path near the broken pillars of a lost temple.

parameters: A few pillars remain intact, but the ancient temple has been reduced to a pile of rubble. There is nothing of interest here.
You spend some time in the garden, hoping to discover something useful.
You spend some more time in the garden. At this point, it seems like you're scraping the bottom of the barrel.

narrative: The sun is shining above the temple garden. Lethargic and carefree, the pipe-smoking druid exhales one cloud of smoke after another.
Ruinous walls form a partial enclosure around the temple garden on the eastern plateau. Minding his own business, a cloaked druid is smoking a pipe near the entrance to a dark cavern.
You walk the garden path near the broken pillars of a lost temple. Aside from the familiar druid guarding the cavern, there is no one else here.

parameters: A few pillars remain intact, but the ancient temple has been reduced to a pile of rubble. There is nothing of interest here.
You spend some time in the garden, hoping to discover something useful.
You spend some more time in the garden. At this point, it seems like you're scraping the bottom of the barrel.
Rolling his eyes, the druid shrugs. "Leave me alone."

narrative: It's too dark in here. You need a torch.

parameters: The flames disperse the previously impenetrable darkness within the cavern. Revealed by torchlight, ancient stairs descend into depths unknown.

narrative: The flames disperse the previously impenetrable darkness within the cavern. Revealed by torchlight, ancient stairs descend into depths unknown.
You notice that it's relatively quiet further down the hallway, which remains unguarded – at least so far.

parameters: There is no one behind you.

narrative: You hear the gentle sound of a wordless and harmonious chant, echoing through the illuminated hallway.

parameters: It sounds like the mysterious chant is being performed by a congregation of women.
There is no one behind you.

narrative: Leaving the third chapel behind, you begin to approach the end of the hallway, which is shrouded in darkness.

parameters: The walls are completely bare in this section of the hallway, displaying no further hieroglyphic inscriptions.
There is no one behind you.

narrative: The chapel is empty. The walls are decorated with wolf hides. A strange, angular stone has been placed on the pulpit.
You have returned to the empty chapel where you found the angular stone. The walls are decorated with wolf hides.

parameters: The stone is covered with miniscule inscriptions.

It's a tetrahedron, cut from limestone. Each side displays a set of symbols or letters from four different languages, two of which are unfamiliar. However, you do recognize the hieroglyphs and the common runes of Tem Khiris.

label: Try to make sense of it

parameters: It's a cipher stone. The signs are organized in such a way that the stone may be used for the purpose of translation. You can use it to interpret the hieroglyphs. This is remarkable, considering the secretive nature of druid culture.
You take the stone from the pulpit. There is nothing else to be found here.

narrative: You have discovered the entrance to another chapel, where a different mosaic adorns the opposite wall. Judging by the silence, there doesn't seem to be any activity within the second chapel.
It's quiet near the entrance to the second chapel.

parameters: The mosaic depicts a wolf leading a procession of humans from a burning city.

narrative: The dark chamber reeks of putrefaction. Chains hang from the ceiling, displaying the flayed skin of a dead cultist. The walls are decorated with an abundance of raven masks.

parameters: There is nothing here but piles upon piles of skeletal remains, reduced to spinal fragments and cranial shards, broken like the residual pottery of lost cities.
You hide the body in a corner of the room.

narrative: You emerge from the dark chamber. A cloaked woman stands in the hallway, armed with two daggers. Her face is concealed behind a circular white mask. "You might be able to fool the others, but not me. Any last words, thief?"
Exhausted, you lean against the bloodstained wall, looking down at her battered corpse. Unfortunately, the commotion has attracted the attention of others. They quickly overwhelm you.

parameters: It's no use. You are shackled and thrown into a cell. Years go by, until the druids decide to sacrifice your malnourished body to the rooks on Triad Apex.

narrative: You retreat into the dark chamber. The masked druid is right behind you.

parameters: You're too slow. Outmaneuvered in the shadow by a whirlwind of blades, your body is riddled with cuts and stab wounds.
Moving swiftly, you step around the corner. You strike low, wounding her right leg. She trips and falls headfirst, giving you the upper hand.

narrative: Broken, battered and bruised – the cunning druid has been thoroughly defeated.
You have discovered the entrance to a third chapel, where yet another distinct mosaic adorns the opposite wall. The wordless chant is being performed by a congregation inside the chapel.
The echoes of a wordless and ethereal chant resonate near the entrance to the third chapel.

parameters: The mosaic depicts a woman with nine burning heads. She is standing within a teardrop inside the sun.
Soothing and harmonious, the wordless chant is beautiful. You wonder if anyone would disagree.
You could stand here all day. The chant almost lulls you to sleep.

narrative: As you walk down the serpentine path from Triad Apex, you have feeling that you're being watched.
A wolf is prowling in the wilderness nearby. Momentarily, you lock eyes with the predator. The wolf begins to move closer.

parameters: It's too late. Failing to outrun the savage predator, you are struck down as the wolf leaps at you from behind, gnawing at your throat. Tumbling downhill, you finally escape its relentless jaws. Back on your feet, you bleed from the neck as you stand face to face with the growling animal.

narrative: You make a run for it. It sounds like you're being pursued downhill by some kind of creature.

parameters: You're being chased by a wolf. The savage beast is closing the gap, step by step.

narrative: You have slain the beast. The dead wolf lies bleeding and twitching in the tall grass.
The gateway to the bridge is closed.

parameters: The gates won't budge, no matter what you try.
There is no discernible locking mechanism. You don't even know where to start.

narrative: Downstairs, there is a dark entryway to a prison. The iron gate is closed.

parameters: It doesn't work, no matter how hard you try.

narrative: Where would you like to go?
The front door is missing. There are faded hieroglyphs above the entrance.
The second floor was the stage for your act of mass desecration. You left the white shrouds in one pile and the naked corpses in another.
The stench from the cauldron is unbearable.
You have returned to the kitchen on the ground floor. The stench from the cauldron is unbearable.

parameters: There's no way to access the second floor from here, as it has been sealed off. The bricks from the staircase have been repurposed to enclose the fire pit.

narrative: The interior of the dusty old tavern has been painted with a fresh coat of blood.
The first floor dormitory is empty. There is nothing here but broken furniture and old junk.
A rainstorm howls across the grasslands of Roe. You travel south until you discover a small military encampment.
The foggy grasslands of Roe are quiet and barren. Nothing is heard aside from the steady trickle of rain.
The bandit camp reeks of death. There is no one else here.
The campsite is littered with rotting corpses. There are no signs of life here.
A stench of rot has descended on the camp between the two rivers. There is no one else here, for now.
You begin to explore the city ruins. Based on your first impression, the buildings have been uninhabited for a long time. There's a cavern nearby.
The sunlit ruins of Dusk Megalith are located on a mountainous plateau, overlooking the forest highlands to the south.

parameters: The ceilings have mostly collapsed. Some of the more prominent structures have recently been used as makeshift stables. You discover a path beyond the ruins to the north. It will take you to the summit.
You discover a short flight of stairs on the eastern outskirts. The stone steps will take you to a garden below, which surrounds the fallen pillars of a lost temple.

narrative: Seemingly deserted, the log cabin stands alone on the eastern shore. The door has been left ajar.
The northern path takes you downhill into a forest valley. You hear the fluttering of wings when a murder of crows takes flight above the trees.
You have returned to the northern valley. Sunrays breach the mist of the forest.

You delve deeper into the valley, noticing footprints in the dirt where the undergrowth has been cleared. It seems like a group of people has wandered this path not too long ago. Further down the slope, you catch sight of large hole in the ground. Hardly a natural formation, the pit provides an abrupt ending to the forest path.
Once again, you find yourself wandering the lower depths of the northern valley. The forest hills are shrouded in fog. Further down the slope, the path leads to a wide pit, which is clearly man-made.
As you move closer to the edge of the pit, you hear faint cries of desperation from below: "Anybody? ... Please... I'm trapped down here... Please, I can't take it much longer..."

parameters: There is no clear path to follow beyond the pit. Realizing that you might lose yourself in the foggy wilderness of the valley, you are left with no other choice but to turn back.

narrative: You ascend the rising cliff path until you reach the summit, where the smuggler's hideout is enclosed by a tall palisade. The gate is unguarded.
You grab your shovel and start digging. One by one, you unearth the caskets. You may now reap the fruits of your labor.

label: Wipe the sweat from your brow

narrative: You have entered the office of Hadrian Trout. Hunched over his marble desk, his attention is focused on the large amount of scrolls and documents in front of him.
You're standing in the office of Hadrian Trout. Hunched over his marble desk, his attention is focused on the large amount of scrolls and documents in front of him.
You’re standing in front of the entrance to the parlor house, which is a white marble building. Rosebushes are lined up along the path to the front door.
Downstairs, you discover a hall of doorways. Marked with numerals, stone doors lead to private living quarters.
The hallway is quiet and nebulous. Private living quarters are locked behind every stone door, marked with numerals.

parameters: The hallway is quiet and nebulous. There are ten doors on each side, numbered from one to twenty. The stone doors are locked, without exception. You discover a descending staircase at one end of the hallway. At the other end, you discover a bright passageway.

narrative: Which door would you like to unlock?

parameters: No matter which door you try, it seems that the locking mechanism is too advanced. You would have to acquire more sophisticated tools in order to disable the locks in this corridor.

narrative: You try the key that you took from the assassin. The iron key fits and the stone door is unlocked.
You approach the stone door.
On the other side, you discover a dormitory. There are eight bunk beds, three wardrobes, a couple of chairs and a sturdy iron strongbox.
Inside, there is a dormitory with eight bunk beds, three wardrobes, a couple of chairs and a sturdy iron strongbox.

parameters: You find a green cloak inside the wardrobe.
The wardrobe is empty, aside from a small parchment.
The iron strongbox is locked. You don't have the key.
You grab the cloak from the wardrobe.
The floor is dusty and the chamber pots reek.

label: Pick the lock on the strongbox

parameters: You fail in your attempt to disable the lock.

narrative: The silent forest is a dark void. Having lost all sense of direction, both of you collapse from exhaustion, convinced that you have fled to safety. Stargazing below the full moon, you are overwhelmed by a sense of relief, as the owls resume their brief proclamations.
You wake up at dawn. Feeling cold as you watch the cloudless sky, you realize that Rasleen is elsewhere. A loud, constant noise resonates in the distance.

parameters: Horses, chariots and marching infantry – it sounds like an army has been set in motion.
You’re standing on top of a hill. Looking around, you catch a glimpse of the ocean between the pines.
For a brief moment, you gaze across the vast emptiness beyond the northern shore. Here, the forest hill is abundant with fruits and berries, ripe for the picking.

narrative: As the noise grows louder, you catch sight of Rasleen. The nomad is perched behind some bushes, watching the ruckus below.

parameters: Indeed, a long procession of chariots, infantry and mounted cavalry is moving on a narrow ledge overlooking the rift valley. The men and women are all dressed in green cloaks and heavily armed. They seem to be heading south.
"This is our chance. Come on." Keeping her head low, the nomad gets moving.

As you catch up with her, Rasleen explains: "Been trying to figure out where the druids are hiding their ship. They must have mobilized their army somewhere nearby. If we're lucky, that's where we'll find it."

narrative: The troops are crossing a sandstone bridge from the east. The high arches rise above the rift valley.

parameters: On the other side of the bridge, druid infantry emerge from the gateway of a ruinous pylon. Above, standing stones crown the summit, partially obscured by lush foliage.
Keeping a safe distance, you wait quietly until the last warriors have marched by. "Dusk Megalith," Rasleen whispers.

"Heard about it. They say it started as a burial mound and grew from there. But people say all kinds of things," she mutters. "Look." She directs your attention to the standing stones at the top. "Triad Apex of Dusk Megalith. Couple of thousand years old, I reckon."

She nods, impatiently. "That's what they call it." Her eyes dart back and forth. "Listen… war's brewing on the Isle of Dusk. Not a good idea to stick around. If we're gonna steal the ship, this is the perfect time to do it."
The scarred nomad glares at you. "Pay attention. Focus. Time and place for everything."
"The Triad are three gods... the ones druids worship. So they've got three stones up there. Apex, 'cause it's the highest point on the island... and that's it."

narrative: "From here on out, keep your eyes open and mouth shut. Some druids probably stayed behind."

Without exception, the same raven masks and feather patterns adorn the lifeless bodies on the ground. Slumped forwards with her back turned towards you, the lone woman is doubly armed with sword and spear, using the latter as a crutch.

parameters: Like a wild-eyed whirlwind, the woman rapidly turns around to face you with a hostile demeanor. Despite being drenched in blood from top to bottom, her features are distinct enough. She was one of the prisoners on the ship – of this you are certain.

Scarred and disfigured beyond belief, this young woman is quite short and remarkably lean. She has dark brown eyes and auburn hair, keeping the latter at bay with a crew-cut.  You remember those eyes, wide and forlorn. Among the cages below deck, they shone like beacons of sorrow.
Lowering her weapons, she nods with a bewildered expression. "Yes… I remember now. You came in with the last batch. The name's Rasleen. I'm a nomad from the Phenris Woodlands."

narrative: "Sure, ask away."

parameters: "This is the Isle of Dusk. Some call it the Isle of Godhead. Doesn't matter what you call it, if you ask me. The island is... merely a shadow, drenched in the blood of innocents."
"Cultists, locked in eternal war against the druids. Never speak, feel no pain. Judging by what I've seen, the latter is definitely true. The Apostles of Woe. Hated by everyone."

label: Know anything about the people with green cloaks?

parameters: "Yeah, those are druids. Conservative bunch. Keep to themselves."

label: You seem to be headed north. Why?

narrative: Seeking cover behind trees and bushes, you move towards the cavern. The entrance is guarded by a druid.

You strike him in the back of the head. Cursing, the druid gets up on his feet, staggering momentarily. Despite his likely concussion, he is quick to retaliate.
You strike him in the back of the head, not once but twice. Groaning and cursing, the druid gets up on his feet, staggering aimlessly.

Despite your best effort, you're too weak. Awakened from his lethargic state, the druid plants his left knee in your face, which leaves you with a fractured nose bone. Tumbling backwards, a fountain of blood is gushing from your nostrils.
You've got him in a tight grip, but time is of the essence.
Apparently, it's not as easy as it looks. The guard breaks free. Out of breath, he reaches for the halberd and prepares to attack.

It's quite the ordeal. As you struggle to maintain your fatal clutch around his throat, the guard is repeatedly bashing your ribcage with his elbows. Finally, you squeeze the life out of him. Exhausted, you collapse next to the corpse.
It was merely a ruse. Having played dead for a moment, the guard gets back up on his feet, reaching for the halberd.

narrative: The captain's quarters can be found in the back of the ship. Having opened the door, you enter the sparsely furnished cabin.

parameters: There's a table and a chair next to a sturdy bed. Rasleen lies curled up on a bedroll. Wrapped in a blanket, the nomad is shivering.
As you sit down in the chair, Rasleen becomes aware of your presence. Drenched in cold sweat, the nomad struggles to speak: "There you are. You did well, my friend."
"Terrible, to be honest. According to Ato Triasteen, it's likely that I'll never fully recover, because the poison was allowed to linger for too long."

narrative: Coughing, she replies: "Yeah. Suppose I have a confession to make."

parameters: "Where to begin? Knowing that your mind is afflicted, I have to ask… are you familiar with the plight of the nomads?"

"Times are hard for the nomads of Tem Khiris. Our suffering is twofold. The rising city-states devour the ancestral lands of our peoples. The abolition of slavery gave rise to a black market, fed by the slave poachers who hunt our kind, as we remain unprotected by the law."

narrative: She nods. "Do you know about the recent war in the Phenris Woodlands?"

parameters: "My homeland was the last refuge of nomads on the western highlands of Tem Khiris. For more than a century, my people resisted the city-state of Roeburgh. Last year, there was a massive uprising. We struggled to evict the occupying force from the Phenris Woodlands, once and for all."

"We lost." She sighs. "The Roeburgh Militia gave us a choice: exile, conscription or death. Most were exiled to the Deadlands of Triniset. Some chose death and were executed on the spot. A few traitors became soldiers in the Militia."
Rasleen shrugs. "I was already on the run. Their triumphant ritual of humiliation was described to me afterwards."

narrative: "My tribe was always the most militant and independent among the nomads in the Phenris Woodlands. When our lands had been conquered by the city-state of Roeburgh, I had no trouble adapting to life as a fugitive."

parameters: "I was making a living as a mercenary in the Town of Sickle. When I settled a blood feud between rival families, my ruthless efficiency caught the attention of a crime lord named Mantis. He approached me in a tavern, wearing a black cloak…"

"Relax, we have plenty of time on our hands." Rasleen coughs. "As I was saying, the crime lord named Mantis approached me. Attached to his black cloak was a silver brooch, just like the one you found on the beach."
"That's exactly right. At the time, the symbol seemed vaguely ominous. Unable to recall where I had seen it before, I dismissed my suspicions and accepted his job offer."

"It's the unfortunate truth. Much like yours, my mind is afflicted. Unlike you, I've had plenty of time to reflect and put my broken memories back in order. The affliction of the mind is what delayed this confession, nothing else."

"Long story short, I did a few jobs for Mantis. Murder for hire, extortion – that sort of thing. The targets were rival factions in the opium trade. Having done similar work for other smuggling networks in the past, I had no qualms about my employers. Until their true nature was revealed…"

"The business relationship turned sour when I rendezvoused with Mantis on the Arrowhead Peninsula, where his crew had a secret harbor. They were waiting for me, standing in front of a caravel. The Stingray was emblazoned across the purple sails. Mantis invited me to come aboard."

Rasleen nods. "I had gained his trust. Aboard the ship, Mantis showed me the caged prisoners. He revealed some facts about his organization, explaining how slaves and opium were their bread and butter. I was offered to join, on the condition that I round up a few slaves. Naturally, I refused..."

parameters: "That's right. I don't know what they did to us aboard the caravel. Whatever they did, the purpose was to bury their secrets. I have wrestled with the stingray in the realm of thought. I know certain things. These things can now be brought to light..."

"I remember where I first saw the accursed symbol. You see, my tribe roamed the western part of the Phenris Woodlands, a place called Talonbark Ridge. When slavery was abolished, a clan of slave masters built a secret fortress in the region. The Stingray was represented in their coat of arms."

label: What was the name of this clan?

parameters: "We never knew. Besides, this was before my time. As the story goes, their slave poachers were relentless. My people drove them out. As a child, I roamed the secret fortress, where I laid eyes on this heraldic symbol."

label: Was it the same exact symbol?

parameters: "No. The silver brooch depicts one stingray, while the coat of arms had two of them. For my ancestors, it signified the risk of enslavement. For me, it was merely a faint echo of a violent past."

narrative: "Before I was imprisoned aboard the caravel, Mantis revealed the name of his organization: the Khiris Cartel. He also explained that he had business to conduct on Roe Island."

parameters: "Indeed, that's where we're headed. Unless I'm mistaken, the caravel took a detour to drop him off on a beach not far from the Town of Set." Trembling, she adds: "These memories are painful. I need to rest. You should do the same, comrade."

data.name: Set Harbor Encounter: A Fisherman and his Daughter

narrative: As you leave the druids and their stolen galley behind, you hear a loud and repetitive noise nearby.
A fisherman and his daughter are hard at work repairing their small boat, which lies upside down near the water. The two of them barely acknowledge your presence.

parameters: The old man wipes the sweat from his brow. “Yes? Can I help you, stranger?” He gives you a worried look. “You’re not here to rob me, are you?”
He smiles: “Well, that’s a relief. You never know these days. So, what’s on your mind?”

“That’s a short trip. You can’t see it now because of the fog, but Graefir Island lies on the other side of Crone River.” The fisherman points to the west. “Calvino the Boatman should be able to take you there for a small fee.”

“You know what? That’s a good question. I haven’t seen him for a while.” He sighs. “Pirates usually leave him alone, since he provides a crucial service to everyone. But… it’s possible that the bandits got him. It wouldn’t surprise me.”
“Don’t mention it. Good luck to you.” The old fisherman and his daughter resume their work. A light drizzle of rain falls on the harbor of Set.

narrative: A trail of dead bandits leads to a ravaged campsite near a lake. The nomads are gathered around their tribal elder, who is giving a speech to celebrate their victory against the lawless marauders.

parameters: “A few. Less than expected, however. Crossing the river from the south gave us the element of surprise.”

narrative: “We shall travel to the Town of Set. Hopefully, the locals will accept us, now that we have brought peace to Roe Island. Besides, we are looking forward to meet our beloved Rasleen… we thought that she had perished in the war.”

parameters: "Be seeing you, fellow traveler." The crowd of nomads depart, heading north.

data.name: Roe Militia Camp Encounter: Lone Survivor

narrative: It seems like the militia field commander is the last man standing. Trembling and breathing heavily, the weary soldier is surrounded by the severed limbs of ill-fated nomads. He exclaims: "Hold it right there! Don't step any closer!"

Ignoring his command, you walk toward the militia soldier. Enraged by this provocation, he struggles to raise the blood-soaked claymore. Staggering, he secures the massive blade with a firm, two-handed clutch. Charging toward you, he roars: "For the glory of Roeburgh!"

parameters: You have slain the last of the militia soldiers in the camp. Various fluids leak from his twitching corpse, adding to the abundant rivers of blood.

narrative: Without warning, you draw the bowstring and take aim. The weary soldier has no time to react. The projectile hits him in the gut, bypassing the protection of his chainmail cuirass. Staggering, the field commander groans in pain as he struggles to raise his blood-soaked claymore.

parameters: You have slain the last of the militia soldiers in the camp. Various fluids leak from his twitching corpse, adding to the abundant rivers of blood.

narrative: Keeping your distance, you manage to convince him of your peaceful intentions. The soldier seems willing to hear you out.

parameters: "Take a wild guess. The nomads... they attacked without warning. And now... everyone is dead. Except me."
"No... surprisingly, I am unscathed. It will take a while before my soul recovers, however."
The field commander mumbles to himself: "...women... children... not what I signed up for...".

"I don't know..." Lost in thought, the soldier wanders off, allowing his claymore to rest on his left shoulder. You watch the weary soldier disappear into the mist, his tattered mantle billowing in the wind.

narrative: There is no one else around. A great multitude of dismembered corpses are gradually submerged in puddles of rain.
You have returned to the militia camp, which lies abandoned. The campfire is no longer burning. Numerous corpses rot in the mud.

parameters: You probe the abandoned tents and dead bodies in search of anything valuable.

narrative: Guided through the fog by cries of anguish, you discover a couple of prisoners. They are trapped in small wooden cages, half-buried in the mud of a long trench. Battered and bruised, the prisoners languish among the bones of dead slaves.

parameters: Both of the caged prisoners are middle-aged men. One bears the marks of a war veteran, the other is a crooked hunchback with a wispy beard. Half-conscious, their glances betray desperation and plead for mercy.

narrative: You break open their cages. Staggering, the two prisoners ascend from the mud. Having had time to adjust, they express their gratitude. The tall, scarred war veteran introduces himself as "Chief Hadrian Trout, mayor of Set", while the crooked hunchback is named "Calvino the Boatman."
Soaked in rain, the quavering seafarer explains his predicament: "I have suffered for too long by the hands of the Tusk Mob... please, make it quick, so that I may return to Set before dusk."

label: Tell me about the Tusk Mob

parameters: Shaking his head, he croaks: "Wild bandits, nothing more... they have carved out a path of destruction on Roe Island."
"The stingray. I've seen their ships. People whisper about the Khiris Cartel."

label: What do you know about the Khiris Cartel?

parameters: "I am wise enough to know that they should not be trifled with. Beyond that, I'd rather not know. You'd be better of asking Chief Hadrian Trout. He's a man of the law, after all."

label: Can you take me to Graefir Island?

parameters: Calvino nods. "Of course. Seek me out in the Harbor of Set."

narrative: Standing tall, the aged war veteran speaks: "I was captured by the Tusk Mob during my investigation of their criminal enterprise. They've kept me here for days. The Roeburgh Militia will be in your debt, stranger."

label: Tell me about the Tusk Mob

parameters: Looking around, Hadrian replies: "They're history, judging by recent events." Chuckling, he adds: "Jokes aside, they are a bunch of roving bandits, armed by the smugglers from the Isle of Bast. Recently, they've been eager to please the higher strata of crime lords, hoping to amplify their underworld status..."

label: What can you tell me about the Isle of Bast?

parameters: "It lies east of here, across Delph River. The ruins and dead forests are home to smugglers, bandits and wild boars. Not the most hospitable place, you might reckon."
Scrutinizing the artifact, Hadrian furrows his brow. "The insignia of wretched crime lords, spawned by the exiled slave masters of Khiris Cartel."

label: What do you know about the Khiris Cartel?

parameters: "Too much. Their history runs deep. A rising star in the underworld of opium and slavery, which spans across the four corners of Tem Khiris. Come visit my office near the Wolf Shrine of Set. The extent of my knowledge is contained within my reports."

label: I am searching for a crime lord named "Mantis"

parameters: He sighs wearily. "Again, once you have read my reports, your curiosity will be satisfied. For now, I must retire to my office in Set."

narrative: The scarred military commander bows. "Farewell." Heading north, Hadrian departs.

"Praised be Phenris." Before leaving, he adds: "I can take you to any of the neighboring islands, for a small fee. You can find me in the harbor of Set." The hunch-back staggers away, soon devoured by the mist.

data.name: Roe Lake Path Encounter: Lone Fisherman

narrative: As you head south to the lake, you cross paths with a wandering fisherman. He warns: "Don't go any further. It's dangerous out here."

parameters: He replies: "Ruthless bandits roam the area. Their encampments have expanded on both sides of the northern river."

He shrugs. "I've been fishing in these waters for many years. On this day, I return empty-handed, simply out of fear. The Tusk Mob wants to conquer this island, it seems... and Lake Roe is the main source of clean water."

label: I see. Thanks for the warning

parameters: He nods. "Don't mention it." Clearing his throat, the fisherman adds: "I really must get going, but let me give you a final piece of advice. The bridge across the northern river is guarded by several bandits. If you must venture forth, then proceed with caution. Farewell, traveler."

narrative: "Suit yourself, traveler." The fisherman goes on his way. You walk alone on the foggy plains. The waters of Lake Roe lies ahead.
The fisherman goes on his way, eventually disappearing into the mist. You stand alone on the foggy plains. The waters of Lake Roe lies ahead.
Frightened, the fisherman squirms, pleading: "The bandits have already taken everything... please, if you let me go, I will never speak of this again!"
You have brutally slain the harmless fisherman. A precious heirloom was tucked away underneath his bloodstained wool shirt.
Rain pours from the gray skies above the waters of Lake Roe. A rushing river flows east.

data.name: Roe Path Encounter: Bandit Camp (Stealth or Force)

narrative: A group of bandits are guarding the bridge across the northern river.
A group of bandits are guarding the bridge across the northern river, which forms a natural divide between their two encampments.
Brandishing their knives, no less than five thugs are blocking your way. One of them says: "You're in the wrong place. This territory belongs to the Tusk Mob. Leave now, before you get hurt."
Brandishing their knives, no less than five thugs are blocking your way. One of them says: "You again? Didn't I tell you to stay away? Fool."

You move silently through the mist as you approach the riverbank. Crouching down among the reeds, you remain undetected as the bandits patrol the bridge above. They are no more than dark silhouettes from this vantage point.

parameters: Your arrow hits one of the bandits in the throat. Grimacing, he falls off the bridge with a splash, adding a touch of crimson to the rushing river below. The other bandits hurry to take cover on both sides of the bridge. So far, you remain safe in your hiding place among the reeds.

The rushing river is cold. You lack the physical fortitude, resulting in catastrophe. It doesn't take long before your life is claimed by the strong current. Helplessly, you descend into icy darkness - out of breath, out of time.

You make it across the river, despite the cold grip of its icy current. Exhausted and soaked in saltwater, you stand on your knees on the gravel. Coughing and wheezing, you feel the cold edge of a blade as it severs your artery. Blood gushing from your throat, the world fades as you collapse on the riverbank, watching a bandit wipe off his blade as he slips away into the mist.

The projectile is buried in the chest of a roaming bandit, whose bewildered expression is petrified by the clutch of death. In search of the unseen aggressor, vengeful thugs encircle you among the reeds, forcing you to escape.

narrative: Bleeding, the lifeless bandit falls headfirst into the river. It doesn't take long before you are faced with another knife thug. Armed with two daggers, he screams: "I'll slit your damn throat!"

parameters: Another bandit is devoured by the rushing river. Breathing heavily, you feel the growing rush of adrenaline as you stand on the wooden bridge, which is now drenched in blood. Undeterred, yet another bandit approaches with hostile intent.

Cursing, the bandit collapses in a pool of blood. You step over the fresh corpse. Having made it halfway across the bridge, you are faced with another opponent. This one is a lumbering brute, armed with massive butcher knife.
Severely injured, the brute falls backwards. Paying no heed to his fallen comrade, a scarred knife thug steps toward you with a murderous gaze. "This is it. End of the road."
Suffering from numerous wounds and fractures, the fifth bandit finally plummets into his watery grave below. Having defeated the bridge guards, you now stand on the other side of the northern river.

Exhausted, you take a moment to breathe, quickly realizing that the encampment is populated by more bandits. Perhaps intimidated by your herculean effort, they keep their distance, whispering among themselves.

A war cry echoes across the misty plains. Cowering near their tents, the outlaw spectators gasp in anticipation. Armed with sword and shield, a fierce warrior emerges from a straw hut in the distance. The crowd cheers as he begins to charge towards you.
Your swift arrow hits him in the left thigh, but it doesn't seem to slow him down. Roaring savagely, the warrior keeps advancing.

Blood gushing from his throat, the warrior collapses in the mud. Terrified by your martial prowess, the other bandits escape from the encampment. But you are not alone. From out of nowhere, a scantily clad concubine leaps towards you, clutching a sharp dagger. Enraged, the woman screams: "You killed him!"
You deliver a fatal blow to her forehead, cracking it open. A final death rattle can be heard as the half-naked woman tumbles in the dirt.

narrative: As you pull back the bowstring and take aim, the bandits near the bridge become aware of your presence, quickly taking cover on both sides of the river.

parameters: Nowhere to run, nowhere to hide. Wherever you turn, knife thugs encircle you on the misty plains.

narrative: Swiftly, you make it across, despite the force of the icy currents. Masked by the noise of the rushing river, you take cover among the reeds, not far from the inner circle of tents in the camp.

parameters: Quietly, you prowl in the mist until you reach the center of the encampment. Showing no sign of hostility, a shady figure approaches near the campfire. The man whispers: "Don't worry... we met before. I'm one of the prisoners from Dusk Megalith."

He whispers: "When we arrived in the Harbor of Set, it seemed pretty clear who was running things around here. I joined up with the Tusk Mob. All things considered, however... I owe you my life. So let me give you a piece of advice."
The escaped convict motions toward a straw hut beyond the campfire, whispering: "Inside, the war lord rests with his concubine. Slay him, and the Tusk Mob will scatter like a swarm of burned rats."
"Easier said than done, I know." Slipping away into the mist, the fugitive adds: "I'll spread the word, in case you prevail."
You walk past the campfire and reach the entrance to the war lord's domecile. Armed to the teeth, he sleeps on a bed of boar hides, calmed by the embrace of his concubine.

label: Kill him before he wakes up

narrative: You set fire to the interior walls of the straw hut. The flame of your torch soon engulfs the sleeping war lord and his mistress. Their screams resonate as they leap toward you, clutching their weapons in desperation.

parameters: Brief moments pass before the injured war lord hits the ground. Burned and furious, the scantily clad concubine lunges at you with a sharp dagger.
Bleeding, the woman screams in agony as she falls backwards, stumbling on the corpse of her master.

You back away from the burning hut, watching the flames devour it in a matter of seconds. The other bandits escape in droves, bearing witness to the rising pillar of smoke and the stench of charred flesh.

narrative: You awaken the war lord. Rising to his feet, he exclaims: "Your death waits on this side of the river. Your path to the underworld is fraught with dishonor. The gods will judge you accordingly."

parameters: Weak in the knees, the injured war lord collapses. Enraged, his concubine leaps forward to strike you, clutching a sharp dagger.
Bleeding, the woman screams in agony as she falls backwards, stumbling on the corpse of her master.
Triumphant, you emerge from the straw hut. Soaked in blood, you hear the whispers of fearful bandits. Knowing that the head of the snake was severed, they struggle to escape the encampment.

narrative: You crush his throat, leaving him to face death in the realm of dreams. Enraged, his concubine leaps to her feet. Clutching a sharp dagger, she delivers a quick slash across the side of your face.

parameters: Bleeding, the woman screams in agony as she falls backwards, stumbling on the corpse of her master.

narrative: You crush the throat of his sleeping mistress, quietly and swiftly. Her death rattle is a mere whimper, provoking no response from her master.

parameters: You disembowel the sleeping war lord. Shocked, he awakens in violent convulsions, unable to contain the flight of his entrails. Twitching, he dies beside his lifeless mistress.

parameters: Inhuman laughter echoes across the landscape of molten rock. As you struggle to ascend the cliffs, you realize that you are being stalked by a four-legged predator. The pale monstrosity plummets into the darkness below. Bones crack repeatedly as the whimpering beast falls from one rock to another.
There is no escape. Guttural and repulsive, the incessant laughter grows louder and louder until the creature is gnawing at your ankles.

narrative: You swiftly ascend the cliffs, ignoring the incessant cackling behind you. Nearly exhausted, you eventually manage to outrun the strange creature. Taking a moment to catch your breath, you can still hear the guttural laughter somewhere in the distance behind you.

Carrying the torch, you are a lone beacon of light in the subterranean wasteland. Taking long strides as you retrace your steps across this forsaken landscape of molten rock, it doesn't take long before you return from whence you came. Standing tall in front of you, the Hollow Gate beckons.

Years of neglect has rendered most of the structures unusable. There's an old barn with a collapsed roof. The granary is nothing more than a pile of rubble. But the farmhouse in the center is still standing. You catch a glimpse of movement in one of the broken windows.
You have returned to the frontyard of the farmhouse. Again, you catch a glimpse of movement in one of the broken windows. You are likely being watched.

As you turn around to leave, you suddenly feel a painful sensation in your left leg, so intense that you collapse headfirst in the mud. A barbed arrow is lodged in your thigh. You hear the sound of footsteps approaching.

parameters: You struggle to get up, but the pain in your leg is more than you can handle. A hooded militia soldier approaches. Raising his sword, he inquires: "Any last words?"
"Quit your whining. It won't help ya." The hooded soldier stabs you repeatedly with his sword, until you suffer a remarkably painful death.
"I like the quiet ones. Your death will be swift and dignified." Keeping his word, the soldier decapitates you with one forceful swing of his blade.

narrative: Despite the pain, you manage to rise to your feet and turn around. A hooded militia soldier approaches. "What are you doing here? Did Hadrian send you?"

parameters: "Hm. I might be willing to talk, on two conditions..." Having cleared his throat, he goes on to say: "I want to get paid. And I want to be left alone. Don't follow me. Don't rat me out."

I promise to let you go

parameters: "You know what? I don't trust you. Get the hell out of here before you get hurt."
Somewhat hesitant, he replies: "Good. Now, the money... Gimme a hundred gold and I'll tell ya where those creeps are hiding."

Having counted the coins, Arturo says: "Listen. People like me aren’t allowed anywhere near their headquarters, but… I’ve seen it from afar. There’s a great tower on the Isle of Bast, you can’t miss it. When you get there, go all the way to the top… and look to the north. You’ll see what I mean…”
"Then you're wasting my time... I won't cross the Tusk Mob unless you make it worth my while."

narrative: It was a tough fight, but you finally prevail. Severely injured, Arturo yields: "You got me, fair and square..." Bleeding profusely, he falls to his knees. "Let's work something out..."

parameters: "Listen... People like me aren’t allowed anywhere near their headquarters, but… I’ve seen it from afar. There’s a great tower on the Isle of Bast, you can’t miss it. When you get there, go all the way to the top… and look to the north. You’ll see what I mean…”

parameters: It's no use. You're severely injured. Before you know it, your throat is pierced by another projectile. As the world darkens, you hear the sound of footsteps approaching.

parameters: You charge forward to attack, provoking the soldier to launch another arrow. This one hits you in the eye, traveling all the way to the back of your skull. As you fall to your knees, you hear him muttering: "Told ya to stay put. Imbecile..."

narrative: You quietly enter the farmhouse. Armed with a bow and arrows, a hooded soldier stands near one of the windows. He doesn't seem to be aware of your presence, as his attention is focused on the frontyard.

parameters: You move silently in the shadows of the derelict farmhouse until you are close enough to reach the hooded soldier.

parameters: The hooded soldier charges toward you, but your projectile hits him above the right knee. It does slow him down, if ever so slightly, but his murderous rage is amplified tenfold. Within seconds, you will be within reach of his blade.

narrative: Startled, the hooded soldier turns around to face you. "Huh? W-what are you doing here?"

narrative: You deliver a devastating blow to the back of his head. Enraged, he turns around, reaching for his blade. He roars: "By the Great Wolf! I will crush every damn bone in your weak body!"
"Pleasure doing business." The corrupt guardsman leaves you alone.

Realizing that you won't change your mind, Arturo remains quiet as you deliver him to the Militia soldiers in the Town of Set. "We'll take it from here. Talk to Chief Hadrian Trout if you want to claim your reward. Farewell, traveler."

The military officer leans back in his chair, folding his arms. "What's on your mind, traveler?"
Chief Hadrian Trout waits patiently for you to speak.

label: I have some questions about your reports...
I am here to claim a bounty

parameters: "Excellent. One less bandit to worry about."
"Good job. Soon enough, these knife thugs will be nothing more than a fading memory..."
"You keep killing 'em, you keep getting paid. That's how it goes."

parameters: "Yes, I was told that you were the one who brought him in. Good work. Here's your reward." Hadrian gives you a pouch of gold.
Hadrian seems disappointed. "Hm. I'd rather have him arrested, but I suppose this form of justice will have to suffice. Here's a little something for you." Hadrian gives you a pouch of gold.

narrative: "Ask away."

label: What can you tell me about the Isle of Bast?

parameters: "It lies east of here, across Delph River. The ruins and dead forests are home to smugglers, bandits and wild boars. Not the most hospitable place, you might reckon."

label: What can you tell me about Graefir Island?

parameters: "It lies west of here, across Crone River. The forest hills are populated by druids and bears. Not much else to say..."

label: What can you tell me about the Roeburgh Militia?

parameters: "The city-state of Roeburgh has two armies. Nobles become knights, commoners become soldiers of the Militia. The knights defend the nobles, while the Militia takes care of the rest..."

label: Why is there no law and order on the islands?

parameters: Visibly frustrated, Hadrian replies: "Don't get me started. Out here, we are left to fend for ourselves, due to the priorities of our leaders on the mainland. Been like this for as long as I can remember... but now is not the time to dwell on the past."

narrative: "Go ahead. I'm all ears..."

label: What do you know about Mantis the Crime Lord?

parameters: "A dangerous man. Story goes, he grew up as an orphan on the streets of Malequiem. Became an assassin at young age, which is how he gained his reputation. Seen him around here many times, but we were never able to touch him. Always surrounded by Cartel enforcers..."

label: Do you know where I can find him?

parameters: "You've read my reports. I can't say for sure, but I believe that he was headed for the Isle of Bast..." Clearing his throat, the military officer adds: "Arturo the Guardsman might know more, but he seems to have disappeared."

label: Tell me more about Arturo the Guardsman

parameters: "Another tale of wasted potential, it seems. Like many others, he came here as a young exile. Very tight-lipped about his past, but that's usually the case. A good soldier, at least in the beginning... until he was tasked with the investigation of the Tusk Mob. That's when things started to go downhill. If you can find him, please bring him to justice..."

"Good question. He's the leader of the Tusk Mob and defacto ruler of the Isle of Bast. Legend has it that the Ironclad Vagrant conquered Bast during the civil wars. But that was a lifetime ago. Some believe that he's immortal. More likely, it's some kind of inherited title..."

narrative: You enter the log cabin. The interior is cluttered with broken furniture and miscellaneous junk. Rainwater drips from the ceiling.
You're standing among the broken furniture and piles of junk inside the log cabin. Rainwater drips from the ceiling.

parameters: As far as you can tell, there is nothing useful to be found in this old house.
At first glance, there is nothing useful to be found in this old house. But things are not always what they seem. Having thoroughly searched the interior, you discover a concealed floor hatch.

narrative: You climb down the ladder to a narrow corridor. The stonework is illuminated by wall sconces. At the other end of the corridor, a large man stands with his arms crossed in front of a sturdy door.
The mustachioed guard observes indifferently as you approach. He mutters: "Never seen you before. Hope you're not lookin' for trouble."
The mustachioed guard observes indifferently as you approach. He mutters: "I recognize you. Never forget a face..."

label: What's on the other side of that door?

parameters: "Place of business. The price of admission is five gold. You in or out?"

The guard shuts the door behind you as you enter the crowded chamber, which reeks of opium and moonshine. A blonde woman greets you with a smile, revealing a full set of golden teeth: "The savior from Dusk Megalith returns! You honor us with your presence. Welcome to our humble den of thieves."

parameters: The crowded chamber is filled to the brim with crates, barrels, chests, sacks and cabinets. About a dozen people are conversing among themselves, drinking and smoking. They all seem to know each other.

Still smiling, the blonde woman explains: "We don't mince words around here. The world is full of arbitrary restrictions. This is a place where supply meets demand. Now tell me, what is it that you desire?"

"Specifically? I'm not sure. We're not good with names." The room erupts with laughter. Wiping a tear from the corner of her eye, the woman goes on to say: "We're just a group of friends who like to stick together. I'm the hostess. That's all you need to know, really..."

The woman keeps smiling as if she's eager to show off her golden teeth: "Well, then you should talk to my good friend over here..." She motions toward a cowled man with an eyepatch. "This is our world-class smuggler, who would prefer to remain anonymous. I'm sure you understand." The one-eyed man greets you with a nod.

The woman seems overly excited. "Look no further! I specialize in all manner of intoxication. Please, have a look at my wares and let me know when you have made your decision. Satisfaction guaranteed!" She winks at you and giggles.
The smiling woman replies: "With all due respect, this is a place of business - not gossip."

Her smiles fades ever so slightly: "Unfortunately, due to the recent influx of savage bandits, most of the whores on Roe Island have been murdered or kidnapped. It's a shame, really. They had quite a reputation!"
Always eager to display her golden teeth, the exuberant young hostess grins: "Make yourself at home, friend."

narrative: The rain subsides as you and Rasleen wander the hills of the forest. “I was out in these woods a long time ago”, she whispers. “I know there’s a path somewhere around these parts.”

label: What were you doing out here?

parameters: “Murder for hire”, she states, matter-of-factly. “Many places to hide for a fugitive… took me a while to track ‘im down.” She sighs. “This is not the time for jibber-jabber. Let’s keep it moving.”

narrative: Knee-deep in wet grass, you hear the wind stroking the branches of the tall firs around you. “Here we go,” the nomad whispers, gesturing towards a well-traveled path through the shadowy forest.

parameters: Wolves howl in the distance. Slowly but surely, the mist is darkened by nightfall. The path takes you to the garden of a dilapidated mansion. “There it is,” Rasleen whispers, “the Ephemeral Lodge.”

parameters: "I have crossed paths with them more than once. Druids, independent from the others - peaceful and isolated. They roam the forest of Graefir Island to the west. I can show you the way to the Ephemeral Lodge. Just let me know when you're ready to leave."

narrative: Much to the disappointment of the children in the crowd, you step forward to interrupt the tales of your scarred comrade. Smiling, the nomad mercenary says: "You have no idea how happy I am to be reunited with my tribal brethren. Thank you, my friend."

parameters: "We have a lot of catching up to do, if you don't mind..."

narrative: "About time. You know, I've been asking around, but the locals clam up whenever the Cartel is mentioned. Can't blame 'em, I suppose... but it's frustrating... I was beginning to lose hope." She takes a sip of moonshine. "Anyway, let's hear what you've got."

Having finished reading the reports, she hands them over, commenting: "Seems like the Cartel is a lot more powerful than I thought... we might have bitten off more than we can chew."

parameters: "Don't get me wrong, those bastards have to pay for what they did to us, some way or other... at the very least, we can take out Mantis. According to Hadrian's report, he was on his way to the Isle of Bast. It's a dangerous place, so... we should prepare for the worst."

label: Understood. I'll let you know when I'm ready

parameters: She nods. "Sounds like a plan. You know where to find me. See you later."

parameters: "Well, remember what happened last time we crossed paths with Mantis? He had us in the palm of his hand... imagine if we find him on the Isle of Bast. For all I know, he can just tell us to go somewhere else... or kill ourselves. Who knows what he's capable of?"

parameters: She nods. "There must be a way."

You have returned to the harbor of Set. Barely visible in the fog, the stolen galley is guarded by two druids. The entrance to the tavern lies nearby.
You walk alone on the harbor of Set. The coastal shantytown is shrouded in gray mist.

parameters: Calvino says: "Don't forget about your nomad friend. Last time I saw her, she was headed for the tavern."

narrative: It's past midnight. A quiet shantytown lies outstretched on the northern coast of Roe Island. The drum quiets down as the rowers make their final effort. You have reached the Harbor of Set.

parameters: The druids are the only ones who stay behind when you set foot on the Harbor of Set. The rest of the crew quickly disperses on the streets and alleyways in the coastal shantytown.

narrative: You see a tall man dressed in a black cloak. Holding a lantern, he stands alone near a dark alley. The wide brim of his slouch hat covers most of his face. Grinning, he says: “Come with me”.

parameters: There is something about his voice. For whatever reason, you find it impossible to resist his command. As the three of you walk down the rainy harbor, the cloaked stranger says: “You have traveled far. You should get some rest.” He points to a nearby tavern.

“You don’t remember?” He chuckles. “She knows. Don’t you, Rasleen?” The nomad trembles with rage, but seems unable to act on it. Amused by her silent frustration, the man grins: “That’s right. Know your place. Do what you’re told. That’s how it goes.”

He interrupts you: “Quiet. You did well, freeing those prisoners. Never thought you’d make it. But now… I must bid you farewell. Go to the tavern. I think you’ll find the accommodations… satisfactory.” The man walks away into the mist, leaving the two of you alone. Rain keeps falling from the night sky.
Visibly upset, Rasleen nods: “Y-yes. That was Mantis, our lord and master. Let’s go to the tavern.”
Eyes wide open, the nomad nods eagerly: “Yes. We must go.”

narrative: The harbor is dark and quiet. You approach the tavern, which is a ramshackle building with two floors. The windows are brightly lit. A sign hangs near the entrance.

parameters: Several dark silhouettes are discernible behind the cloudy glass.

parameters: It reads: "Infirmary". A handwritten note has been added below, which reads: "Currently at full capacity."
